2  ORDER

The petitioner is the 5th accused in Crime No.1021/2024 registered at the Central Police Station,
Ernakulam, for offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC.

The crime is registered on the allegation that the accused, with intent to cheat the 1st informant, made him install an app in his mobile phone and by assuring 40% profit for money invested through the trading app, caused the 1st informant to deposit Rs.3,37,65,000/- (Rupees Three Crore Thirty-Seven Lakh Sixty-Five Thousand Only) in the account of the accused.

The specific allegation against the petitioner is that from out of the amount deposited by the 1st informant, Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs only)
was transferred to his account.

2. Although petitioner's bail application was allowed by the jurisdictional Magistrate as per Annexure 2 order, condition No.2 therein requires the petitioner to deposit an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs only) within three weeks.
This Crl.M.C is filed challenging the said condition.

3. Learned Counsel for the petitioner contended that the 2025:KER:32763 CRL.MC NO. 3374 OF 2025 objectionable condition is impossible of performance and placed reliance on the decisions in Ramesh Kumar Vs. State of NCT of Delhi [(2023) 7 SCC 461)] and Sumit Mehta Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) [(2013) 15 SCC 570] to point out that incorporation of such onerous conditions have been frowned upon by the Apex Court.

entities.text: Ramesh Kumar Vs. State of NCT of Delhi [(2023) 7 SCC 461)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sumit Mehta Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) [(2013) 15 SCC 570]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the Bank has marked lien on the petitioner's account.
4. I heard the learned Public Prosecutor also.
5. A perusal of Annexure 2 order reveals that, sufficient conditions, for safeguarding the interest of the prosecution, have been imposed.
Over and above that, the trial court cannot impose conditions for ensuring recovery of the amount that may become due to the informant.
As held by the Apex Court, conditions imposed while granting bail cannot be unreasonable, resulting in frustration of the bail itself.
For the aforementioned reasons, the Crl.M.C. is allowed and condition No. 2 in Annexure 2 order is deleted.

Sd/-
